chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Musa ibn Umar, from Abi Ali ibn Rashid, who linked it up to al-Sadiq (peace be upon him),

that he said: There are five things which are as I say: Greedy persons have no comfort, and jealous persons have no pleasure, and rulers are not loyal, and liars are not manly, and fools will not become masters.
ai.seo_question: What are the five things Imam al-Sadiq says define the spiritual state of specific character types?
ai.summary: In this concise maxim from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (as) links specific vices to their inherent spiritual deficits, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *akhlaq* (character) as a mirror of inner state. The phrase 'not a foolish person becomes a chief' (la yasuddu safih) highlights the practical political wisdom that leadership requires not just authority but wisdom, a key theme in Imami thought. This enumeration serves as both a moral warning and a sociological observation on the stability of leadership and social trust.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 5-10 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Musa ibn Umar, on the authority of Abi Ali ibn Rashid who linked it up through a chain of narrators to Imam as-Sadiq (MGB), “
There are five things which are as I say. Greedy persons have no comfort. Jealous persons have no pleasure. Rulers are not loyal. Liars are not manly. Fools will not become masters.”
